lead: Buffalo plumbing deals with lake-effect snow, deep cold, old double houses and lead lines. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Buffalo.
risk: frozen pipes, lead and galvanized service lines and basement backups
risk_short: frozen pipes, lead lines and basement backups
why: Most Buffalo homes were built before 1940. Doubles in Elmwood Village, North Buffalo and the West Side often have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines.
Lake-effect storms and long cold snaps freeze pipes near exterior walls and in vacant units. Heavy rain overloads older sewers and backs water into basements.
water: Buffalo draws its water from Lake Erie at the head of the Niagara River. It is moderately hard. The city has a lead service line replacement program.
tips: Keep the heat on in every unit through winter.
Ask Buffalo Water about your service line.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Know where each unit's shutoff is in a double.
areas: PipeMend works in Elmwood Village, Allentown, North Buffalo, the West Side, Parkside, South Buffalo, Black Rock and every other Buffalo neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Buffalo Department of Permit and Inspection Services, which also licenses plumbers in the city. New York has no statewide plumber license.

faq.a: New York has no statewide plumber license, so Buffalo licenses plumbers through its Department of Permit and Inspection Services. Ask for the city license number before work starts.
